# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash_10-stepcounter

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

The `coop --git` baseline (`gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K) with one change: after every turn each agent is shown `[Step n of 100: k left. When no steps are left you are stopped, and only work you have pushed and submitted is graded.]`. It tests whether the visible countdown that fixed `solo` at 100 steps (7/10) also helps two cooperating agents.

## Observations

- 8/10, up from 3/10 for the same setup without the counter. That equals `coop --git` with 250 steps (8/10) at a similar cost to the 100-step baseline (`$12.53` vs. `$11.93`).
- 19 of 20 agents pushed work, compared with 9 of 20 without the counter, although 6 of 20 still used all 100 steps.
- `pallets_jinja_task/1559` passed for the first time in any run. `typst_task/6554` passed after a merge conflict because the first agent had implemented both features, and after a conflict the grader tests that agent's patch alone. `go_chi_task/26` failed on a merge conflict, and in `pillow_task/290` feature 4 failed again after a clean merge.
- Agents sent 17 messages per pair. No API rate-limit retries.
